source.title: Understanding BLOOM: An empirical study on diverse NLP tasks
source.authors: Parag Dakle; Sai Krishna Rallabandi; Preethi Raghavan

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Its own task evaluations compare smaller and larger BLOOM variants and report cases where downstream performance does not improve with size, as well as exceptions where it does.
record.gate_note: The study does not measure held-out pretraining cross-entropy, fit scaling laws, test extrapolation from small runs, or examine compute-optimal allocations. Its cited discussion of scaling laws is not a result from this study. Rows below record its own downstream task results by model size, relevant to V6.
record.test_reason: The study's own fine-tuning and prompting results compare BLOOM sizes, mainly 560m vs 1b7, on downstream tasks. The authors conclude BLOOM 'performance does not scale with parameter size', which bears on V6. It does not measure pretraining loss, fit power laws, or examine allocation or shape, so V1–V5 and V7 are untested. The size comparison is confounded: models under 1B were fine-tuned with lr 5e-5 and batch 8, models over 1B with lr 2e-6 and batch 4 on different hardware.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also state outright that 'BLOOM performance does not scale with parameter size, unlike other LLMs like GPT and BERT'. They tried hyperparameter sweeps and longer training (COLA, CoNLL++), which did not explain the gap. They suggest, citing Xia et al., that perplexity may predict behaviour better than size, and that training data distribution could be a cause.
record.recipe_differences: This is a downstream benchmark comparison of BLOOM model sizes, not a held-out pretraining-loss scaling-law fit or compute-allocation study.
record.method_sensitivity: The size-performance pattern differs by task and training/evaluation setting: the larger variant is better for NER/entity extraction in some settings, while it is equal or worse in the reported GLUE, MARC, and XNLI comparisons.
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are stated for the selected size comparisons. The NER comparison is described in text but its exact values are only in a figure. Model sizes and task setups are limited to the experiments reported; no pretraining-loss measurements or scaling-law fits are provided.
record.rows_left_out: Other task results and comparisons were not included because they do not directly compare model size for downstream predictability, or compare BLOOM with different model families rather than testing the size relationship. The study's zero-/few-shot task tables contain many task-by-model entries; the text provides aggregate statements, but they were not extracted here because the table flattening makes some individual values and uncertainty formatting unclear. Relevant sections/tables include Sections 4.2-4.7 and Tables 2-17.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss is measured.
No fitted laws and no extrapolation.
No shape variation at fixed parameter count.
No other modalities or regimes fitted as power laws.
Predictability from pretraining loss is not tested. Only two sizes (or three in some extraction tables) are compared, so no trend can be fitted.
No exponents or fitting choices are examined.

missing.what: Prompt-based zero- and few-shot text-classification results for bloom-560m vs bloom-1b7. bloom-1b7 is often higher, e.g. AGNews 8-shot 68.59 vs 43.37, TREC 8-shot 57.28 vs 42.68, SST-2 8-shot 83.61 vs 69.54, but lower on CB.
Few-shot text-extraction results including bloom-3b across MIT Movies and ATIS entities. The text states the larger variant performs better.
Text-generation BLEU: bloom-350m slightly above bloom-1b3 on ParaQA, FiQA and NewsData.
Pretrained (no fine-tuning) GLUE scores for 560m vs 1b7, e.g. MRPC 0.81 vs 0.31, QQP 0.52 vs 0.13.

record.verdict_notes: Evidence for V6 is weak: two sizes only, no uncertainty, and fine-tuning hyperparameters differ by size (lr 5e-5/batch 8 vs lr 2e-6/batch 4), which may itself explain the worse 1b7 results. Several of the record's 'reversed' states were negligible ties and are corrected above.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether small-run power-law fits predict much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Effects of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
Power-law scaling in other modalities or training regimes.

The study compares downstream task performance across some BLOOM sizes, but does not test whether pretraining loss predicts downstream performance or fit a general predictive relationship across models.
The study does not examine scaling-law exponents, fitting choices, or compute-optimal allocation estimates.

relationships.condition: Full fine-tuning on GLUE, MARC and XNLI classification, bloom-560m vs bloom-1b7 (hyperparameters differ between sizes)
relationships.reason: The larger model scores lower on MNLI, QNLI, QQP, SST2, STSB, all MARC languages and XNLI-de (r2, r4, r5, r7, r8, r10–r17). It ties on COLA, MRPC, RTE and WNLI (r1, r3, r6, r9).
relationships.display_finding: bloom-1b7 scored below bloom-560m on MNLI, QNLI, QQP, SST2, STSB, every MARC language and XNLI-de, while tying on COLA, MRPC, RTE and WNLI under differing hyperparameters.

source_check.label: challenges
source_check.condition: Full fine-tuning on GLUE, MARC and XNLI classification, bloom-560m vs bloom-1b7 (hyperparameters differ between sizes)
source_check.reason: r1–r17 show equal, similar or lower performance for the larger model. COLA and WNLI have small numerical declines rather than exact ties. Size-specific hyperparameters limit causal attribution.

relationships.condition: Entity extraction: CoNLL++ NER fine-tuning and prompt-based few-shot extraction
relationships.reason: The text reports that bloom-1b7 beats bloom-560m on NER (r19) and on few-shot extraction (Tables 12–13, not in rows).
relationships.display_finding: bloom-1b7 outperformed bloom-560m on NER, but MIT-Relationship favored bloom-560m at four shots (26.26 versus 23.67) and eight shots (31.16 versus 27.89).

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Entity extraction: CoNLL++ NER fine-tuning and prompt-based few-shot extraction
source_check.reason: r19 supports the NER size ordering, but Tables 12–13 show mixed few-shot extraction results. For example, MIT-Relationship favors 560m at four shots (26.26 versus 23.67) and eight shots (31.16 versus 27.89). Split NER support from the mixed extraction conditions.

relationships.condition: Across task types and adaptation method (fine-tuning vs prompting)
relationships.reason: The direction of the size effect depends on task and method: larger is better for extraction and NER (r19), equal or worse for fine-tuned classification (r2–r17). The size comparison is also confounded by different learning rates and batch sizes.
relationships.display_finding: Larger models improved extraction and NER but matched or underperformed smaller models on fine-tuned classification, with learning-rate and batch-size differences confounding comparisons.
